title: Timothy Busfield Accused Of Groping 16-Year-Old Actress During Auditions | Hollywood News - News18
text: Actor Timothy Busfield is facing fresh allegations of sexual misconduct as prosecutors move to keep him in jail ahead of a trial on child sex abuse charges. According to court filings, Busfield is accused of groping a 16-year-old girl during an audition at the B Street Theatre in Sacramento. The new claim comes in addition to previous charges against Busfield, who is currently being held at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Albuquerque, NM. He faces three charges of sexual abuse involving a boy who acted on the Fox show The Cleaning Lady. Busfield’s lawyer has strongly denied all allegations. Prosecutors are pushing to hold Busfield without bail, arguing that he has exhibited a “sustained pattern of predatory conduct." The new Sacramento allegation reportedly occurred several years ago. “While auditioning for the defendant at B Street Theatre, the 16-year-old reported that the defendant kissed her and put his hands down her pants and touched her privates," the filing stated. It added, “The defendant begged the family to not report to law enforcement if he received therapy." Busfield appeared in court on Wednesday via Zoom from jail and a hearing on the state’s motion is expected within five days. Until then, he will remain in custody. Timothy Busfield Denies Allegations Busfield’s civil attorney, Larry Stein, said on Wednesday that Busfield had voluntarily submitted to a polygraph examination regarding the allegations. “Tim Busfield denies the allegations in the criminal complaint and maintains they are completely false," Stein said. The attorney added, “As a voluntary step, he submitted to an independent polygraph examination regarding those allegations and passed." In addition to the new charges, Busfield has faced previous allegations of sexual misconduct in 1994 and 2012, though those did not lead to criminal charges. Warner Bros Accused In Case Timothy Busfield directed six episodes of “The Cleaning Lady," which aired on Fox from 2022 to 2025. Prosecutors have accused Warner Bros, which produced the show, of complicating the investigation, including delaying an internal review of Busfield. “The delayed and limited cooperation by Warner Bros. in responding to a search warrant further underscores the institutional barriers that have historically enabled this type of misconduct to occur," prosecutors wrote. A detective also noted that employees feared retaliation from Warner Bros for cooperating with law enforcement. In response, Warner Bros Television said it did cooperate with investigators and maintained that its policy does not allow retaliation against those raising concerns. Busfield was arrested after a warrant was issued over allegations he groped a seven-year-old boy on the set of the show. Police said the boy reported that Busfield touched his “private areas" on a bedroom set.
